content.value_statement: Website structure decisions affect navigation, search visibility, and content growth. This skill turns business goals into page hierarchies, URL maps, sitemaps, and linking plans.
actual_capabilities: Creates page hierarchy plans for SaaS, content, commerce, documentation, hybrid, and local sites.
Designs header, footer, sidebar, breadcrumb, and mobile navigation patterns.
Recommends readable URL patterns that match page hierarchy and content type.
Produces ASCII trees and Mermaid visual sitemaps for stakeholder review.
Plans internal linking with hub-and-spoke models, contextual links, and orphan page checks.
Generates URL map tables, navigation specs, and task-specific planning questions.
limitations: It does not generate XML sitemaps or resolve crawl errors.
It needs business goals, audience context, and page inventory for precise plans.
It provides planning guidance, not implementation code or CMS configuration.
It does not replace analytics, keyword research, or usability testing tools.

use_cases.title: Plan a New Marketing Site
use_cases.description: Create a clear page hierarchy, navigation model, and URL plan before design or development starts.

use_cases.title: Restructure a Growing Website
use_cases.description: Group existing pages, reduce navigation clutter, and define redirects for pages that move.

use_cases.title: Organize Scaled SEO Sections
use_cases.description: Fit integration, comparison, template, or guide pages into hubs with strong internal linking.

prompt_templates.title: Start a New Site Plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a new website.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan the site architecture for a new [site type] website. The business serves [audience] and the main goals are [goals]. Include a page hierarchy, navigation plan, URL map, and internal linking recommendations.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Current Navigation
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate restructuring for an existing site.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this current page list and reorganize it into a clearer site architecture: [paste pages]. Identify primary sections, secondary pages, header navigation, footer groups, and redirect concerns.

prompt_templates.title: Add Scaled SEO Pages
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced planning for programmatic or content-led growth.
prompt_templates.prompt: We are adding [number] [page type] pages. Show how they should fit into the site architecture, including hub pages, URL patterns, navigation placement, crawl concerns, and internal linking.

prompt_templates.title: Create Stakeholder Deliverables
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced output for design, SEO, and development teams.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a complete site architecture package for [website]. Include an ASCII hierarchy, visual sitemap guidance, URL map, navigation spec, breadcrumb notes, and internal linking plan.

output_examples.input: A SaaS company needs to add features, pricing, blog, integrations, and comparison pages.
output_examples.output: The skill returns a homepage-centered hierarchy, grouped product sections, integration and comparison hubs, concise URL patterns, and header and footer navigation recommendations.

output_examples.input: A content site has 50 pages and users cannot find important resources.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a content inventory, new section groups, flatter navigation, before and after structure notes, redirect planning, and internal link priorities.

output_examples.input: A team wants a visual sitemap for design review.
output_examples.output: The skill provides Mermaid-ready sitemap guidance, clear page relationships, navigation zones, and supporting notes for wireframes and stakeholder review.

best_practices: Provide audience, business goals, site type, and important pages before asking for a plan.
Ask for both hierarchy and navigation deliverables when design and SEO teams must align.
Include current URLs when restructuring so redirect and breadcrumb risks are visible.
anti_patterns: Do not ask it to fix XML sitemaps, crawl errors, or technical SEO implementation.
Do not approve a new hierarchy without checking important pages and user paths.
Do not mix unrelated URL patterns across similar page types without a clear reason.

faq.question: What does this skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces page hierarchies, URL maps, navigation specs, visual sitemap guidance, and internal linking plans.

faq.question: Can it create XML sitemaps?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on information architecture and navigation planning, not XML sitemap generation or crawl diagnostics.

faq.question: Which website types does it support?
faq.answer: It supports SaaS marketing sites, content sites, commerce sites, documentation, hybrid sites, and small business sites.

faq.question: Can it help with a redesign?
faq.answer: Yes. It can reorganize current pages, define before and after structures, and flag redirect needs.

faq.question: Does it include visual diagrams?
faq.answer: Yes. It can provide Mermaid sitemap guidance and text-based hierarchy formats for planning discussions.

faq.question: What information should I provide first?
faq.answer: Provide the site type, target audiences, business goals, current pages, priority pages, and URLs that must stay stable.
